item.content:encoded:
President of the Fiji Law Society, Wylie Clarke will appear on a special episode of fijivillage Straight Talk With Vijay Narayan at 5.30pm today.

The show will focus on Clarke's personal experience after he faced serious allegations against him in the Commission of Inquiry report on the appointment of FICAC Commissioner, Barbara Malimali, months of chaos and struggles for him and his family, natural justice not afforded to him and other co-applicants in the case, and the eventual High Court decision declaring the COI report null and void in its entirety.

There are also several revelations in this afternoon's special show.

You can watch the show on our facebook page, X, TikTok and YouTube channel, fijivillage.

You can also catch the podcast, fijivillage Straight Talk With Vijay Narayan on Spotify and Apple Podcasts.

item.title: Second suspect arrested in Howell Road temple sacrilege case
item.description: Police have arrested an 18-year-old man believed to be the second suspect involved in the Howell Road temple sacrilege case. The suspect is currently being questioned by Samabula Police as investigations continue into the incident where money and other items were stolen from a temple along Howell Road.
item.content:encoded:
Police have arrested an 18-year-old man believed to be the second suspect involved in the Howell Road temple sacrilege case.

The suspect is currently being questioned by Samabula Police as investigations continue into the incident where money and other items were stolen from a temple along Howell Road.

The first suspect, a 17-year-old juvenile, appeared at the Suva Magistrates Court earlier today.

More than $900 was recovered by the investigation team during their inquiries.

According to a temple committee member, $2,000 was stolen on Monday morning.

Police investigations into the matter are continuing.

item.title: Fijian designers Temesia and AZA to showcase at NZ Fashion Week
item.description: Two Fijian designers will take the Pacific fashion story to the international stage when they showcase their collections at New Zealand Fashion Week 2026. Temesia Tuicaumia of TEMESIA and Zulfikar Ali of AZA will present their designs this evening, with support from the Trade and Investment Office - Fiji High Commission New Zealand and Kahui Collective.
item.content:encoded:
Two Fijian designers will take the Pacific fashion story to the international stage when they showcase their collections at New Zealand Fashion Week 2026.

Temesia Tuicaumia of TEMESIA and Zulfikar Ali of AZA will present their designs this evening, with support from the Trade and Investment Office - Fiji High Commission New Zealand and Kahui Collective.

TEMESIA, founded by Tuicaumia , is known for combining modern tailoring with traditional Fijian motifs, creating designs that reflect heritage, identity and innovation.

For NZFW 2026, TEMESIA will present “Waves of Legacy”, a collection inspired by the ocean’s importance to Pacific life and the strength of Fijian culture.

Tuicaumia says the collection is a tribute to ancestors and aims to create new conversations in fashion.

He says preparing for the international runway came with challenges, including sourcing sustainable materials and adapting to international standards, but the experience helped push his creative boundaries.

Meanwhile, AZA, led by Zulfikar Ali, will showcase “Island Prism”, a collection highlighting the connection between light, tradition and modern design.

Ali says his goal is to showcase Fiji’s vibrant aesthetic and challenge perceptions of Pacific fashion globally.

He says the journey involved overcoming logistical challenges, refining designs for an international audience and balancing cultural authenticity with global appeal.

The designers’ participation is being supported through a partnership between the Trade & Investment Office - Fiji High Commission New Zealand and Kahui Collective, which has provided access to resources, mentorship and industry networks.

Tuicaumia says the opportunity is not only about showcasing clothing but also about sharing Pacific culture and inspiring future generations of creatives.

Ali says NZFW provides a platform for Fijian stories to be seen and celebrated.

Their participation highlights the growing presence of Pacific designers on the global fashion stage and strengthens creative connections between Fiji and New Zealand.
